_readme: Cross-document queries: questions no single document in the corpus answers.
Run with `make eval-crossdoc`, or
`python scripts/eval_retrieval.py --queries config/eval/retrieval_queries_crossdoc.json`.
WHY THEY ARE A SEPARATE SET. They measure a different thing, and mixing them
into the main set would average the two into a number describing neither.
The main set asks 'is the answer ranked first' and MRR is its metric; this
set asks 'is the answer ASSEMBLABLE from the top five' and complete@5 is
its metric. Recall is the lenient reading of the same question: one of two
required documents is recall 0.5, and an answer that is half-evidenced is
not half right -- it is confidently wrong, which is worse than missing.
COMPLETE@5 COUNTS EVERY DOCUMENT GRADED ABOVE ZERO. It is exactly
'recall@5 reached 1.0', with no hidden threshold deciding which grades are
required. The consequence is the rule for writing a query here: a document
that is NOT needed for a complete answer is graded 0, which records that it
was considered and rejected. Grades 1 and 2 are not 'optional' -- they say
how much a document contributes to nDCG, and they still have to be found.
WHAT MAKES A QUERY BELONG HERE. Remove any graded document and the question
should be answerable only worse or not at all. That is stricter than
'relevant', and it is what stops this file becoming a way to raise the
ceiling by listing everything on a topic.
THE DOCUMENTS ARE THE ONES ADDED AS DISTRACTORS, and that is the finding
rather than a shortcut. A second document on a topic is noise when the
question is narrow ('how many days of annual leave') and essential when it
is broad ('what happens to my unused leave when I resign'). Relevance is a
property of the query-document pair, never of the document -- which is why
the corpus marks them 'role': 'secondary' rather than 'distractor', and why
'distracts' names the query they distract FROM.
THE CEILING RISES HONESTLY HERE. These queries have two or three relevant
documents because the corpus really does split the answer that way, not
because somebody wanted P@5 above 0.2.
EVERY QUERY IS ANSWERED BY DOCUMENTS IN ITS OWN LANGUAGE, and that is a
constraint rather than an accident. BM25 shares no token between 中文 and
English, so a Chinese query with English gold documents scores exactly zero
however good cross-document assembly is -- it measures cross-lingual
matching instead, which is a different question and a different metric.
x-07 was written that way at first and returned nothing at all; see its
note. Cross-lingual retrieval needs a multilingual embedding, so it belongs
in a set `eval_full_pipeline.py` runs.

queries.query: 我和配偶两个人加起来一共可以休多少天产假
_note: 158 days and 15 days live in different documents and the question asks
for the total. Neither document is sufficient and both are necessary,
which is the cleanest possible case of the category.
Also the adversarial one: these two documents are the pair BM25 already
cannot separate (q-15's recorded limit), so a retriever that confuses
them scores well HERE for the wrong reason. That is worth having --
a metric nobody can accidentally pass is not the same as one nobody can
accidentally fail.

queries.query: do service accounts and user accounts follow the same password rules
_note: A comparison, so both sides are necessary by construction: one document
says service accounts rotate every ninety days, the other says user
passwords are not rotated on a schedule. Either one alone answers 'yes'
or 'no' wrongly.
This is the shape `_comparison_plan` and the `compare_entities` skill
exist for, and nothing in the evaluation set exercised it until now.

queries.query: I spent 250 dollars on a team dinner, what do I need to claim it back
_note: The meal rule gives forty dollars a day without an itemised receipt; the
approval rule catches anything above two hundred. A reader given only the
first would conclude the receipt is optional, which is wrong at this
amount -- so the second is necessary, not merely useful.

queries.query: what happens from the moment a severity one incident is detected until it is closed
_note: Paging within five minutes is the start, the postmortem within five
working days is the end, and the question asks for both ends.
Note both documents contain 'severity one' and 'five', which is the
lexical trap: a retriever can get both for the wrong reason. complete@5
does not distinguish those, and does not claim to -- it says the evidence
was there, not that it was found for a good reason.
Notice and handover are both necessary steps. The annual-leave payout is
graded 2 rather than 3 because it is a consequence of resigning rather
than a step in the process -- but it still counts toward complete@5, per
the rule above, because a resignation answer that omits what happens to
unused leave is incomplete. Ceiling 3/5 = 0.6.

queries.query: how do we know a backup from last month can actually be restored
_note: Thirty-day retention is one half and quarterly restore drills are the
other, and the answer is the interaction between them -- a month-old
backup is still there, and drills are the reason to believe it works.
Neither document says anything about the other.

queries.query: 公司有哪些培训，分别什么时候考核
_note: New-joiner security training is assessed within three months of
joining; the annual compliance training is assessed every December.
Two kinds, two deadlines, two documents, and the question asks for
both -- neither document mentions the other's training.
**This query replaced one that could only ever score zero, and the
replacement is the point.** The first version asked 新员工入职第一周
需要完成什么 and its gold documents were onboarding_laptop.md and
onboarding_accounts.md, which are in ENGLISH. BM25 shares no token
across the two scripts, so it returned nothing at all -- measured,
rank '-'. That is a real limit of this corpus (its Chinese and
English halves are lexically disjoint) but it is a limit on
CROSS-LINGUAL matching, not on cross-document assembly, and this set
exists to measure the second. Leaving it in would have dragged every
aggregate down for a reason the set does not name -- the same
argument this file makes for not merging itself into the main set.
Cross-lingual retrieval is what a multilingual embedding is for, so
it belongs in a set the full-pipeline harness runs, not here.

queries.query: 年假没休完又要离职，怎么处理
_note: Carry-over to the end of March and the three-times payout on departure
are different documents and the question sits exactly between them.
The application procedure is graded 1: somebody deciding whether to take
the leave before resigning needs to know it takes five working days'
notice. A 1 rather than a 2 because it shapes the decision rather than
answering it -- and it counts toward complete@5 either way, which is the
rule this file states once rather than per query. Ceiling 3/5 = 0.6.
